name: Router as DHCP Server
brief:
LAN 10 is addressed by hand and LAN 20 is meant to be automatic. Configure R1 as the DHCP server for 192.168.20.0/24, reserve the bottom ten addresses for infrastructure, and hand clients a gateway and a DNS server along with their address.

Then switch PC2 to DHCP and prove it got a working lease.
watchFor: Exclude addresses BEFORE you create the pool. The router hands out the lowest available address, and if you have not excluded the gateway it will happily give it away.

tasks.hint: `ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.20.1 192.168.20.10` in global configuration mode.

tasks.text: Create a DHCP pool named LAN20 for the 192.168.20.0/24 network.
tasks.hint: `ip dhcp pool LAN20`, then `network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0`. Notice the prompt becomes (dhcp-config)#.

tasks.text: Set the default gateway option to 192.168.20.1.
Set the DNS server option to 192.168.10.50.
Switch PC2 to DHCP and confirm it received an address.
tasks.hint: Use the IP Configuration panel on PC2, or run `ipconfig /renew` at its command prompt.

tasks.text: Run ipconfig /all on PC2 and read back the address, gateway and DNS server it was handed.
On R1, confirm the lease with show ip dhcp binding.
From PC2, ping PC1 at 192.168.10.20 to prove the lease is usable.

extension: Predict which address PC2 will receive before you renew it, and say why. Then release and renew twice and see whether the router hands back the same one.
debrief: DHCP hands out four things, not one: address, mask, default gateway, DNS server. A client with an address but no gateway looks configured and reaches nothing beyond its own subnet — a failure mode worth recognising instantly, because `ipconfig` shows it in one line.
